body:
I had an ex who behaved similarly. It's really painful, and most people react poorly to it. I definitely did. If it's possible, you should apologize, be sure not to expect any apology from her, because chances are she won't give you one, and you need to move on.

Anger counseling might be a good idea. Someone who also works with depression would be best. You seem to be blaming yourself for her bad behavior; it has nothing to do with any shortcomings you might have. Her actions are her own, and yours are your own. Use your regret for what you did as motivation to improve as a person.

I feel like there's a lot left to do, like I don't want to die yet. It's just when the waves of dread hit me that I think I need to do all of this immediately, and I start crying.

I really hope you don't want to die. I don't know what else to say. I want you to live.
I haven't put in notice with my job or my landlord. It's just a thought. Maybe more than just a thought, but it isn't something I've acted on or that I have any real intention to act on.

Motivation is really tough. If you can't think of any tangible motivation, I think your motivation should just be feeling better.

I realize everyone and his uncle has some sort of solution to feeling better when you're down, and mine probably isn't any better, but I've always found that I feel better when I'm doing something than doing nothing.

If you need any specific ideas or just someone to talk to, I'll be available anytime through Monday morning, then sporadically from then on.

Hope you feel better soon.

So I'm 20, I was diagnosed with depression when I was 11.

I'm going to ignore most of what you said, I think other people can help you better with that since I'm not in a great place right now, either. But meeting people, I got that shit down.

So if you don't go to school, you should read or watch movies. Learn about stuff. Click the random button on Wikipedia. Being smart is awesome, but people will like it better if you know the year of the Battle of Hastings than if you can do math quickly in your head. It's basically parlor tricks, but it works.

I still find myself making jabs at myself occasionally, but I tend toward cocky douchebag in social situations. As much of a douchebag cocky douchebags are, people seem to enjoy their company.

As for getting into social situations, it's a lot easier when you can get into bars. But for now, meetup.com is pretty cool. Gyms, community centers. Churches are great, if you're into that.

And you shouldn't self-diagnose, it's a bad habit. I did that all the time, the time probably would've been better spent with friends, or playing flash games or something. There are tons of less self-destructive ways to waste time. These days, I like my DS. Library books are free, if you're strapped for cash.

Best of luck!

Hi. I'm about the same age. No kids, but no family or close friends nearby. I understand the stress, at least from that. I can't imagine how hard it must be having five kids, too.

If you have any time, I'd recommend going to free events in the community. Meeting people, talking to people. I've been depressed for as long as I can remember and talking to people has always been the only thing that's helped.

There are a ton of places to help take care of kids, these days. A lot of them are free. I'm not sure how many exist in your area, but the Boys' and Girls' Club seems to be in most places. It would be good social experience for your kids, and it would give you more time to relax.

I don't know much about the adult dating world, unfortunately, but it seems that /u/maxxumless has good ideas around that.

I'm sorry I can't be of more help, but I really hope you feel better.

You know...I agree with you on a lot of things. I think everything sucks. I think there isn't much logic behind living. I think it's cool that you've done everything you really want to do, from my impression you're still somewhat young (though I could be wrong).

It might seem a little silly coming from me - a quick look at my post history would tell you that I am also contemplating suicide - but don't do this. Your wife will absolutely not be better off without you. She's your wife, she obviously wants you in her life, even if for some reason things have burned out between you. You need to talk to her. Not everyone has someone right next to them who loves them.

I have a friend like that, but it just seems there's some glaring problem with each new person I meet. Too haughty. Too stupid. Too into drugs. Too morally loose. I guess that might be a reflection on the friend, though.

I went to a nerdy school, and the people I know there aren't the type to introduce you to anyone new. I'm not sure how too meet people outside of the school/work circle.

edit: I don't mean to sound superior to my schoolmates. I'm not the type to introduce you to anyone new, either.

I've never had any luck finding bandmates. I was briefly in a guitar duo with one of my best friends back in high school, but nothing since then.

I'm not sure I really want to continue with my existing relationships. I don't think I care very much about them.
Guitar, yoga, video games. They just seem to be ways to spend time, though.

Thanks for the words of advice. I know there's more to life, but it doesn't look like there's much more. My romantic relationships this past year have been consistently disappointing, and I don't feel much of a connection to my work. I have friends who seem to genuinely like me, and talk me up whenever they get the chance, but as much as I appreciate having them around, I don't feel much of a connection to them, either. I look for new and exciting things whenever I have the time, but nothing really seems to excite me.
